nodes.label: Airbnb Design System Analysis
nodes.rationale: A token-based extraction (colors / typography / rounded / spacing / components) of Airbnb's consumer-marketplace system, kept as a structure-only reference.

nodes.label: Rausch (#ff385c) — Single Brand Voltage
nodes.rationale: One accent color carries every primary CTA, the search orb, the heart save state and brand links. Used scarcely — pages are ~90% white + ink with one or two Rausch moments — which is what makes it recognizable.

nodes.label: Airbnb Cereal VF Type Scale
nodes.rationale: A single variable font carries display, body, nav and micro copy — no separate display family. Display weights stay modest (500-600 at 22-28px) rather than the 700+ of fintech/enterprise systems. Inter is the documented open-source substitute.

nodes.label: Photography-Led Visual Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: The system trusts photography and whitespace for visual heft instead of typographic muscle — which is WHY the homepage h1 sits at only 28px/700 and the listing h1 at 22px/500. The single loud typographic moment is the 64px rating display, because rating numbers are the peak trust signal.

nodes.label: Soft Shape Language (rounded scale)
nodes.rationale: 8px buttons, ~14px cards, fully-pill search bar, circular orbs/hearts. There is essentially no hard corner anywhere except the body grid — every interactive element is rounded, which reads as friendly and human.

nodes.label: Single Elevation Tier
nodes.rationale: One shadow definition plus a flat baseline — no progressive elevation tiers. Depth comes from photography, white-on-white surface separation and rounded-corner clipping instead of layered shadows.

nodes.label: Pill Search Bar + Rausch Search Orb
nodes.rationale: 64px fully-rounded white bar split by hairlines into Where/When/Who segments, terminated by a 48px circular Rausch orb — the hottest single color moment on the homepage and the most-tapped target.

nodes.label: Photo-First Property Card
nodes.rationale: 1:1 photo with rounded clipping, carousel dots, 'Guest favorite' badge top-left, heart top-right, then 4-5 meta lines. property-card-photo is split into its own token because wishlist/search surfaces reuse the photo plate without the meta block.

nodes.label: 64px Rating Display
nodes.rationale: The only place the system trusts type alone to carry hierarchy. Stars render in ink (#222222), not gold — a deliberate choice because yellow stars read as cheap in a travel context.

nodes.label: 8px Spacing System & Density Contrast
nodes.rationale: Sections get 64px of vertical air (tighter than the 80-96px typical of SaaS marketing) while card grids compress to 16px gutters — 'open hero, dense marketplace below'. Marketplace pages need card density per scroll.

nodes.label: Three-Product Top Nav (Homes / Experiences / Services)
nodes.rationale: Hand-illustrated 32px glyphs plus 'NEW' badges on the two newer products — signals a marketplace expansion rather than a feature dump.

nodes.label: Luxe / Plus Sub-Brand Accents
nodes.rationale: Luxe purple (#460479) and Plus magenta (#92174d) are scoped to sub-branded surfaces only and never appear in mainline marketing — preserving Rausch as the single brand voltage. Their full sub-systems are a documented gap.
